nfl.oneThing: Puka Nacua has gone on injured reserve with a knee and toe injury and will miss at least four games, a major blow to the Rams (5–4) and their passing game.

headlines.title: Nacua headed to injured reserve
headlines.summary: The Rams placed Puka Nacua on injured reserve on Thursday, a day after Sean McVay had said he would stay on the active roster. Nacua hurt his right knee and a toe in the 20–13 win over Washington and was diagnosed with MCL and PCL sprains and turf toe. He will miss at least four games, and the earliest he can return is December 20 against Dallas. In seven games he had 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns, and ESPN Research says his 70 receptions are the most through a player's first seven games in NFL history.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Rams are 5–4 and one game back of the seventh seed in the NFC. Davante Adams is already on injured reserve, so the receiving group is thin.

headlines.title: Vikings welcome Cousins back as leader
headlines.summary: The Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders just before Tuesday's trade deadline, in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick. His first full day back went well, with Justin Jefferson saying it was a joy to see him lead in the meeting room. Minnesota (6–2) lost 23–6 to Buffalo on Monday night, and Cousins replaces Kyler Murray as the starter. He has 20 passing touchdowns this season, second in the league behind Joe Burrow's 23.
headlines.whyItMatters: Minnesota are 6–2 and sixth in the NFC.

headlines.title: Steelers and Bengals meet for the AFC North lead
headlines.summary: Pittsburgh and Cincinnati are both 6–2 and meet on Sunday night with the AFC North lead on the line. Both teams are on four-game winning streaks. CBS Sports has made the case for an upset, pointing to Pittsburgh's rest advantage and its defence. Cincinnati's Joe Burrow has been on a strong run during the winning streak.
headlines.whyItMatters: Both teams are in the AFC playoff picture, with Cincinnati sixth and Pittsburgh fourth. The result will reshape the division race.

nba.oneThing: Stephen Curry will miss at least two weeks with an oblique tear, and the Warriors are bracing for closer to a month. That changes the picture for their NBA Cup game against the Spurs on Friday.

headlines.title: Curry out at least two weeks with oblique tear
headlines.summary: Stephen Curry will miss at least two weeks with an oblique tear, according to ESPN, and the Warriors are bracing for him to be out closer to a month. Curry is averaging 27.8 points per game, fourth in the league. Golden State is already without Brandon Williams, Kristaps Porzingis, Moses Moody and Jimmy Butler III. ESPN's Tim MacMahon says Yaxel Lendeborg needs to become the go-to scorer while Curry is out.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Warriors are 8–4 and sixth in the West. They face the Spurs on Friday in NBA Cup group play without their star.

headlines.title: Marcus Smart suspended three games for punch
headlines.summary: The NBA suspended Rockets guard Marcus Smart three games without pay for throwing a punch at Warriors centre Charles Bassey during Houston's 115–108 win on Wednesday. The right hook grazed Bassey's nose in a late third-quarter confrontation, and Smart was assessed a flagrant foul 2 and ejected. He will miss games against Utah on Friday, Washington on Sunday and Miami on Monday. Smart joined Houston in free agency and is averaging 8.6 points over nine games.
headlines.whyItMatters: Houston are 9–3 and third in the West, so the suspension will test their depth over the next three games.

headlines.title: Caleb Wilson out 4–6 weeks with fractured hand
headlines.summary: Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson will have surgery on a fractured right hand and is expected to miss four to six weeks. He was hurt in the first half of Wednesday's loss to the Spurs. The fourth overall pick in the 2026 draft is averaging 19.3 points and 6.3 rebounds. Chicago are 1–9 and have lost eight straight.
headlines.whyItMatters: CBS Sports says the injury will likely end his chances in the Rookie of the Year race. Chicago have little to build on at 1–9.

headlines.title: Lakers keep rolling with Doncic
headlines.summary: The Lakers beat Milwaukee 123–112 for their seventh straight win, and they lead the West at 11–2. Luka Doncic is averaging a league-leading 38.6 points per game. Sandro Mamukelashvili scored 23 points against the team that waived him after 1.5 seasons. The Lakers and Spurs are battling for the West lead.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Lakers are first and the Spurs second in the West, so the race at the top of the conference is tight.

recaps.text: Portland beat Oklahoma City 118–108 in a meeting of two winning teams. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander kept the Thunder in it, but Portland's guards decided the game. Deni Avdija and Jrue Holiday were the difference, and the Blazers move to 8–3.

recaps.keyLine: Lendeborg 25 pts, 10 reb, 0 ast · Podziemski 22 pts, 6 reb, 4 ast · Durant 20 pts, 4 reb, 5 ast · Sengun 19 pts, 13 reb, 9 ast
recaps.text: Houston beat Golden State 115–108 in the game that led to Marcus Smart's suspension. Amen Thompson's transition basket with 21 seconds left in the third quarter extended the lead, and Smart and Bassey then squared up. Alperen Sengun was the quiet engine for the Rockets, and Yaxel Lendeborg kept the Warriors close without Curry.

recaps.keyLine: Wembanyama 32 pts, 9 reb, 1 ast, 5 blk · Harper 18 pts, 6 reb, 10 ast, 4 stl · Smith 23 pts, 4 reb, 3 ast, 5 3PM · Claxton 17 pts, 6 reb, 1 ast
recaps.text: The Spurs came back from 14 points down in Chicago to win 124–119 and extend their winning streak to 10. Victor Wembanyama was the headline, but Dylan Harper's playmaking and De'Aaron Fox's passing kept the offence moving. The Bulls had their chances and couldn't hold the lead.

recaps.keyLine: Murray 30 pts, 4 reb, 8 ast · Jokic 27 pts, 11 reb, 8 ast · Jerome 22 pts, 2 reb, 5 ast · Wells 22 pts, 2 reb, 1 ast, 5 3PM
recaps.text: Denver won 123–118 in Memphis in a close game. Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokic did the bulk of the scoring, with Cameron Johnson adding 23 points. Cedric Coward and Ty Jerome kept Memphis within reach, but the Grizzlies couldn't get over the line.

recaps.keyLine: Tatum 24 pts, 7 reb, 8 ast · White 19 pts, 1 reb, 7 ast, 4 blk · Walter 17 pts, 3 reb, 1 ast, 5 3PM · Graves 13 pts, 5 reb, 0 ast
recaps.text: Boston beat Toronto 98–93 in a tight, defence-led game. Jayson Tatum and Derrick White were the key players at both ends, and White's four blocks stood out. Ja'Kobe Walter's shooting kept Toronto in it, but they couldn't close it out, and the Celtics move to 10–2.
